text: What does hyphal anastomosis contribute to a mycelial network?
choices: It divides the network into isolated, single-walled cells
It permanently halts all cytoplasmic streaming
It is the tip-growth process by which individual hyphae elongate
It fuses hyphae into a true network with cycles and redundant pathways, adding robustness
explanation: Anastomosis is the regulated fusion of compatible hyphae, converting a branching tree into a looped network with redundant routes that are robust to damage and efficient for transport, and it requires molecular self-recognition. It does not isolate cells (choice 0) or stop streaming (choice 1), and it is distinct from tip elongation (choice 2).
